title: Where local reasoning fails on networks of permutation contact
claim: For a connected network of permutation contact with holonomy group H on the witness values W, and any commutative ring R with 1 != 0: (1) the basic (level-2) affine relaxation over R is feasible exactly when 1 lies in the ideal of R generated by the sizes of the H-orbits; so over Q every network is accepted, over Z exactly those with coprime orbit sizes, over F_p those with an orbit size prime to p, and the smallest impossible network accepted over Z has 5 witness values with orbits of sizes 2 and 3; (2) pinning the base witness to u makes the basic relaxation feasible exactly when u is a common fixed point of H, over every R; (3) the level-3 relaxation refutes every impossible network by an integer combination of its equations that reads 0 = 1, valid over every R, and path consistency and level-3 Sherali-Adams refute it too; (4) arc consistency, the basic LP, and BLP+AIP beyond AIP refute nothing beyond what (1) says. Each part is checked on declared instances by explicit certificates verified by substitution.
failure_conditions: A constructed certificate fails substitution: a solution violates an equation, or a refutation leaves a variable or a zero constant.
An instance where the prose classification predicts a certificate that cannot be built.
Disagreement with the exact census HOLES-COHOMOLOGY-20261019-001A-E001 on its instances.
foundation_claim_scope: Which local-to-global reasoning methods detect that a network of permutation contact is impossible. No claim about other CSP classes, Nullstellensatz degree, complexity separations, native structure or physics.

validation.status: checked: prose proofs; check.py builds and verifies by substitution the certificate each proof describes on 469 declared networks (85 rings with every cycle type on 2-5 values, 384 random networks on seven graphs), rejects three broken certificates, and agrees with the census's general solver; no human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with mechanized certificate checks on declared instances; no trusted kernel.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-likely: bijection constraints have bounded width and BLP+AIP equals AIP on balanced templates (Nakajima-Zivny); the orbit-ideal criterion over an arbitrary ring with explicit certificates, and the coprime tie as the smallest integer-fooled case, were not found stated. The coprime arithmetic is the one in Lichter-Pago's counterexample (arXiv:2407.09097), without its robustness to higher levels.
validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-19.
